column1: # Corpus records a gadget-to-JIT handover is known to change, one per line as
# <record name><TAB><class>. Each class is a difference between the engines
# in a result the architecture leaves undefined, not a defect of either: the
# tier switch test fails when a listed record ends the same from every
# handover, so a fix removes its rows in the same change.
# undefined-af-after-logical-op: AF after TEST, AND, OR or XOR is undefined.
# The gadget engine clears it, as hardware does. The JIT, like FEXCore
# upstream, leaves it as the instruction before did, and a handover is the
# one place that instruction can have run on the other engine.
